title: Collection considerations: volume, frequency, quality and cost

videos.script: On Tuesday, Caio asks for the dock sensor readings: every dock, every minute, kept for good. {{request}} It sounds like one decision, and it is really four questions. {{four}} How much? Measure a row on a sample instead of guessing it. An hour of readings says a hundred bytes a row, where the guess was forty. {{volume}} How often? Ask what would change if the data were an hour older. Polling every minute makes fourteen hundred calls a day, and most of them come back empty. {{frequency}} How good? A copy that asks only for what changed can lose a row for good, and nothing complains. {{watermark}} So every delivery is checked at the door, and then counted against the source. {{door}} And at what price? Keeping a year of readings costs almost nothing. A dashboard that rereads all of it every five minutes costs over a thousand times as much. {{cost}} Under all four sits one more question: may we have this data at all? A ride describes a person. {{privacy}} This lesson asks every one of them before the first copy, because each answer moves the others. {{end}}
